alerts.reason: Conagra’s fiscal-year net sales rose (A) despite a 9% volume decline (B). If that volume pressure persists as prior-year pricing gains enter the comparison, quarterly net sales could fall at least 5% within two quarters. The filing gives only an annual sales baseline.

Oil States’ Q2 consolidated revenue grew just 1% (A). Product revenue fell 6% on weaker perforating-product demand and delayed conversion of backlog to sales (C). Despite a larger offshore backlog (B), further shipment delays could push total revenue growth to −5% or lower in Q3 or Q4.

Enphase’s Q2 revenue grew 34% as microinverter shipments rose 55% (A), but U.S. demand slowed broadly (B) and inventory accumulated at distributors and installers (C). Those customers could cut orders while selling existing stock, pushing consolidated revenue down at least 5% year over year in Q3 or Q4.

Black Knight’s Q2 EBITDA and margins (D) imply revenue of about $324 million versus $339 million, down roughly 4.5%. Software’s share rose from 86% to 88% (A), implying a steeper decline outside software. A modest further decline there could take consolidated revenue growth to −5% within two quarters.

Spirit’s Q2 operating revenue grew 4.8%, but yield fell 7.4% and load factor fell 3.1 percentage points (A) as capacity grew 17.4%, ahead of traffic growth of 13.1% (B). If traffic growth slows while excess capacity keeps fares under pressure, revenue could fall at least 5% year over year in Q3 or Q4.
